label: prop:q-game-of-life
title: The quantum Game of Life (q-GoL) as a Toffoli-defined substrate automaton
html:
Proposition. The quantum Game of Life (q-GoL) as a Toffoli-defined substrate automaton

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q and Planck time t_P(q) = 1/\hbar_q. Let \mathcal{L} \subset M be a discrete sublattice of brane points \{p_i\}. Each site carries a qubit |\psi_i\rangle \in \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. The q-Game of Life (q-GoL) is the discrete-time invertible cellular automaton

  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
    \colon  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}}
    \to  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}},
  \qquad
  |\Psi(t{+}1)\rangle
   = 
  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
  |\Psi(t)\rangle.

The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is constructed entirely from q-deformed Toffoli gates acting on Reeb bundle fibres of neighbour sites. The construction requires five properties:

  1. Building block. The transition operator is the q-AND gate:
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \colon  |c_1, c_2, t\rangle
  \longmapsto
  |c_1, c_2,  t \oplus_q (c_1 \wedge_q c_2)\rangle.

The symbol \wedge_q denotes the Hecke-algebra q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q), given in the canonical convention z_D under Stability condition below. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q executes in three Planck steps.

This item previously defined \wedge_q as \Phi(q) = (q-1)(q^{3/2}+q^{1/2}-1)(q^{3/2}+q+1)/2(q+1)^2, which is withdrawn: \Phi is not in the image of the Toffoli construction under any indexing or convention (Toffoli transfer matrix), so it cannot be what \wedge_q denotes.

  1. Superposition. Cell states admit superpositions |\psi_i\rangle = \alpha_i|0\rangle + \beta_i|1\rangle via Hadamard rotations H \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}_{p_i}). The set \{\mathrm{Toff}_q, H\} is universal for reversible computation, in the sense of Bennett, for every q > 0: reversible universality needs the gate to be invertible with a firing target-flip channel, both of which item 4 and the non-vanishing of P_{7,6} on q \neq 1 supply.

Open. This item formerly claimed universality for quantum computation. That is a stronger claim and is in tension with item 4: the standard Toffoli-plus-Hadamard universality theorem is a statement about unitary gates, and \mathrm{Toff}_q is provably not unitary for q \neq 1. Whether a non-unitary invertible gate set can be universal in any quantum sense — and if so which — is not settled in this corpus, and the claim is narrowed to the reversible statement until it is.

  1. Conway's rules as Toffoli circuits. Survival (k = 2, 3) and birth (k = 3) at site i with neighbourhood N(i) are enacted by the composite operator
  \mathcal{U}_i^{\mathrm{rule}}
   = 
  \prod_{\{j_1, j_2\} \subset N(i)}
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \!\left(
    |\psi_{j_1}\rangle,  |\psi_{j_2}\rangle;  |\psi_i\rangle
  \right).

Ancilla qubits encode the neighbour sum. A ripple-carry adder of O(|N(i)|) Toffoli gates computes the binary count k.

  1. Reversibility. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q is invertible, with
  \sigma_i^{-1}
   = 
  \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot \mathbb{1},

so \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is invertible and the automaton is reversible. It is not unitary away from the classical limit: the eigenvalues of \sigma_i are q and -q^{-1}, of modulus \neq 1 for q \neq 1, so no inner product makes \mathrm{Toff}_q unitary, and the Markov trace form is degenerate under the production trace convention. Reversibility in the sense a reversible cellular automaton requires — invertibility of the tick — therefore holds for every q > 0, being a property of the quadratic relation alone and independent of the amplitude signs discussed below; unitarity holds only at q = 1.

  1. Information bandwidth budget. One generation advances in 3 |\mathcal{L}| Planck steps. The substrate bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) = q \eta_q / (q - 1)^2 bounds the generation rate:
  \text{gens / sec}
   \leq 
  \frac{\mathfrak{B}(q)}{3  |\mathcal{L}|}
   = 
  \frac{q \eta_q}{3  (q - 1)^2  |\mathcal{L}|}.

Well-definedness condition. The evolution is well-defined only when the Toffoli diagonal P_{7,7}(q) is positive and the q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q) is non-zero. In the canonical convention z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) the two amplitudes are

  P_{7,7}^{D}(q) \,=\, \frac{q^{3}\bigl(q^{4}+1\bigr)}{\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}},
  \qquad
  P_{7,6}^{D}(q) \,=\, -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1\bigr)}{2q\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}}.

The second amplitude is written P_{7,6}, not \Phi. This is a naming correction only and leaves the criterion above exactly as ruled: \Phi named a specific published closed form that the Toffoli construction does not produce under any indexing or convention, so it is retired as an object rather than re-derived in a new frame (Toffoli transfer matrix), and item 1 of this proposition already records that withdrawal.

For q > 0 the first is strictly positive, having no positive root. The second vanishes exactly at q = 1: the factor (q+1) is positive there, and the sextic q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1 has no positive real root, so the whole zero set on q > 0 is carried by (q-1). The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate value q_0 \approx 1.110.

Non-vanishing, not positivity. The criterion is that the q-AND does not degenerate, not that it carry a particular sign. This is the same condition the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND uses — it turns on P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 — and it is what invertibility of the tick requires. At q = 1 the q-AND vanishes and the braiding ceases to act: that is the classical limit, where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli, and it is the one point the condition excludes.

Strict positivity would be a different and stronger requirement. Under z_D it holds only on 0 < q < 1, since P_{7,6}^{D}(q_0) \approx -0.1438, and would place the substrate outside the well-defined regime. It is not the criterion in force here.

A measurement that strengthens the ruling rather than reopening it. Amplitude positivity was standing proxy for feasibility of the confinement LP. That proxy does not track what it proxies for. Constructing the q-Toffoli as an element of H_3(q) — T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 for the all-proton ordering — and evaluating the LP condition G\vec t(q_0) \geq 0 directly against the production Gram gives strictly positive components, for all eight strand-type orderings (Toffoli LP-stability). So the substrate satisfies LP feasibility as well as non-vanishing; the counterfactual above is exact about amplitude positivity and would be wrong if read as "the LP would have excluded the substrate". Two caveats bound this: the Gram is entrywise non-negative and \vec t is too for the all-proton ordering, so that ordering's positivity is forced by shape (2 of the 8 are trivial in this sense, 6 are not); and \vec t turns negative on 0 < q < 1, the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6} does, so the amplitude sign and the cone condition disagree about which regime is admissible. The regime q > 1 this block once named, and the golden-ratio threshold q_\star = 1/\varphi^{2} from which it was read off, were both artifacts of the excised convention C (see Toffoli LP-stability); under z_D the diagonal has no zero at all and q_\star does not exist.
